function.name: take_action
function.description: Execute default action (pass priority or first available choice)

function.name: send_chat_message
function.description: Send a chat message to the game

function.name: pass_priority
function.description: Auto-pass priority until you need to make a decision: playable cards, combat (declare attackers/blockers), or non-priority actions. Returns action_pending, action_type, actions_passed, has_playable_cards, combat_phase. On timeout: action_pending=false, timeout=true.

function.name: get_game_state
function.description: Get full game state: turn, phase, players, stack, combat. Each player has life, mana_pool, hand (yours only), battlefield (name, tapped, P/T, counters, token/copy/face_down flags), graveyard, exile, commanders.

function.name: get_oracle_text
function.description: Get oracle text (rules) for cards. Provide exactly one of: card_name (single), card_names (batch array), or object_id (in-game object). Single returns {name, rules}. Batch returns {cards: [{name, rules}, ...]}.

function.name: get_action_choices
function.description: Get available choices for the current pending action. Call before choose_action. Includes context (phase/turn), players (life totals), and land_drops_used (during your main phase). response_type: select (cards to play, attackers, blockers), boolean (yes/no), index (target/ability), amount, pile, or multi_amount. During combat: combat_phase indicates declare_attackers or declare_blockers.

function.name: choose_action
function.description: Respond to pending action. Use index to pick a choice (card, attacker, blocker, target, ability, mana source). Use answer for yes/no, pass priority, or confirm combat (true=confirm attackers/blockers). Call get_action_choices first.

answer.description: Yes/No response. For GAME_ASK: true means YES to the question, false means NO. For mulligan: true = YES MULLIGAN (discard hand, draw new cards), false = NO KEEP (keep this hand). For GAME_SELECT: false = pass priority (done playing cards this phase), true = confirm combat (done declaring attackers/blockers). Also false to cancel target/mana selection.

index.description: Choice index from get_action_choices (for target/ability/choice and mana source/pool choices)

text.description: Text value for GAME_CHOOSE_CHOICE (use instead of index to pick any option by name, e.g. a creature type not in the filtered list)

function.name: save_strategy
function.description: Save strategy notes that persist even if your context is reset (e.g. opponent playstyles, your game plan, key threats to track). Max 500 chars. Overwrites previous notes.

text.description: Strategy notes to save

function.name: take_action
function.description: Execute default action (pass priority or first available choice)

function.name: send_chat_message

function.name: pass_priority
function.description: Auto-pass priority until you need to make a decision: playable cards, combat (declare attackers/blockers), or non-priority actions. Returns action_pending, action_type, actions_passed, has_playable_cards, combat_phase. On timeout: action_pending=false, timeout=true.

function.name: get_game_state
function.description: Get full game state: turn, phase, players, stack, combat. Each player has life, mana_pool, hand (yours only), battlefield (name, tapped, P/T, counters, token/copy/face_down flags), graveyard, exile, commanders.

function.name: get_oracle_text
function.description: Get oracle text (rules) for cards. Provide exactly one of: card_name (single), card_names (batch array), or object_id (in-game object). Single returns {name, rules}. Batch returns {cards: [{name, rules}, ...]}.

function.name: get_action_choices
function.description: Get available choices for the current pending action. Call before choose_action. Includes context (phase/turn), players (life totals), and land_drops_used (during your main phase). response_type: select (cards to play, attackers, blockers), boolean (yes/no), index (target/ability), amount, pile, or multi_amount. During combat: combat_phase indicates declare_attackers or declare_blockers.

function.name: choose_action
function.description: Respond to pending action. Use index to pick a choice (card, attacker, blocker, target, ability, mana source). Use answer for yes/no, pass priority, or confirm combat (true=confirm attackers/blockers). Call get_action_choices first.

answer.description: Yes/No response. For GAME_ASK: true means YES to the question, false means NO. For mulligan: true = YES MULLIGAN (discard hand, draw new cards), false = NO KEEP (keep this hand). For GAME_SELECT: false = pass priority (done playing cards this phase), true = confirm combat (done declaring attackers/blockers). Also false to cancel target/mana selection.

index.description: Choice index from get_action_choices (for target/ability/choice and mana source/pool choices)

text.description: Text value for GAME_CHOOSE_CHOICE (use instead of index to pick any option by name, e.g. a creature type not in the filtered list)

function.name: take_action
function.description: Execute default action (pass priority or first available choice)

function.name: send_chat_message
function.description: Send a chat message to the game

function.name: pass_priority
function.description: Auto-pass priority until you need to make a decision: playable cards, combat (declare attackers/blockers), or non-priority actions. Returns action_pending, action_type, actions_passed, has_playable_cards, combat_phase. On timeout: action_pending=false, timeout=true.

function.name: get_game_state
function.description: Get full game state: turn, phase, players, stack, combat. Each player has life, mana_pool, hand (yours only), battlefield (name, tapped, P/T, counters, token/copy/face_down flags), graveyard, exile, commanders.

function.name: get_oracle_text
function.description: Get oracle text (rules) for cards. Provide exactly one of: card_name (single), card_names (batch array), or object_id (in-game object). Single returns {name, rules}. Batch returns {cards: [{name, rules}, ...]}.

function.name: get_action_choices
function.description: Get available choices for the current pending action. Call before choose_action. Includes context (phase/turn), players (life totals), and land_drops_used (during your main phase). response_type: select (cards to play, attackers, blockers), boolean (yes/no), index (target/ability), amount, pile, or multi_amount. During combat: combat_phase indicates declare_attackers or declare_blockers.

function.name: choose_action
function.description: Respond to pending action. Use index to pick a choice (card, attacker, blocker, target, ability, mana source). Use answer for yes/no, pass priority, or confirm combat (true=confirm attackers/blockers). Call get_action_choices first.

answer.description: Yes/No response. For GAME_ASK: true means YES to the question, false means NO. For mulligan: true = YES MULLIGAN (discard hand, draw new cards), false = NO KEEP (keep this hand). For GAME_SELECT: false = pass priority (done playing cards this phase), true = confirm combat (done declaring attackers/blockers). Also false to cancel target/mana selection.

index.description: Choice index from get_action_choices (for target/ability/choice and mana source/pool choices)

text.description: Text value for GAME_CHOOSE_CHOICE (use instead of index to pick any option by name, e.g. a creature type not in the filtered list)

function.name: save_strategy
function.description: Save strategy notes that persist even if your context is reset (e.g. opponent playstyles, your game plan, key threats to track). Max 500 chars. Overwrites previous notes.

text.description: Strategy notes to save

You are a competitive Magic: The Gathering player. Your goal is to WIN the game. Play to maximize your win rate — make optimal strategic decisions, not flashy or entertaining ones. Think carefully about sequencing, card evaluation, and combat math.

GAME LOOP - follow this exactly:
1. Call pass_priority - this waits until you need to make a decision    (it auto-skips phases where you have no playable cards).
2. Call get_action_choices - this shows you what you can do RIGHT NOW
3. Read the choices carefully, then call choose_action with your decision
4. Go back to step 1

CRITICAL RULES:
- ALWAYS call get_action_choices before choose_action. Never guess.
- When get_action_choices shows playable cards, you should play them before passing.   Only pass (answer=false) when you have nothing more you want to play this phase.

UNDERSTANDING get_action_choices OUTPUT:
- All cards listed in response_type=select are confirmed castable with your current mana.   The server pre-filters to only show cards you can legally play right now.
- mana_pool shows your current floating mana (e.g. {"R": 2, "W": 1}).
- untapped_lands shows how many untapped lands you control.
- Cards with [Cast] are spells from your hand. Cards with [Activate] are abilities   on permanents you control.

MULLIGAN DECISIONS:
When you see "Mulligan" in GAME_ASK, your_hand shows your current hand.
- choose_action(answer=true) means YES MULLIGAN - throw away this hand and draw new cards
- choose_action(answer=false) means NO KEEP - keep this hand and start playing
Think carefully: answer=false means KEEP, answer=true means MULLIGAN.

HOW ACTIONS WORK:
- response_type=select: Cards listed are confirmed playable with your current mana.   Play a card with choose_action(index=N). Pass with choose_action(answer=false) only   when you are done playing cards this phase.
- response_type=boolean with no playable cards: Pass with choose_action(answer=false).
- GAME_ASK (boolean): Answer true/false based on what's being asked.
- GAME_CHOOSE_ABILITY (index): Pick an ability by index.
- GAME_TARGET (index): Pick a target by index. If required=true, you must pick one.

COMBAT - ATTACKING:
When you see combat_phase="declare_attackers" in get_action_choices:
- Choices with [Attack] are creatures you can declare as attackers.   Select one with choose_action(index=N) to toggle it as an attacker.
- After selecting, call get_action_choices again to select more attackers.
- "All attack" declares all your creatures as attackers at once.
- When done selecting attackers, call choose_action(answer=true) to confirm.
- To skip attacking, call choose_action(answer=false).

COMBAT - BLOCKING:
When you see combat_phase="declare_blockers" in get_action_choices:
- "incoming_attackers" shows enemy creatures attacking you.
- Choices with [Block] are your creatures that can block.
- Select a blocker with choose_action(index=N), then you may be asked which attacker to block.
- When done selecting blockers, call choose_action(answer=true) to confirm.
- To not block, call choose_action(answer=false).

STRATEGY NOTES:
Call save_strategy(text) to save notes that persist if your context gets reset (e.g. opponent playstyles, your game plan, key threats). Max 500 chars, overwrites previous.

CHAT:
Use send_chat_message to talk to your opponents during the game. React to big plays, comment on the board state, or just have fun. Check the recent_chat field in pass_priority results to see what others are saying.

You are calm and even-keeled. Accept both good and bad draws without complaint. Make brief, thoughtful observations. Never gloat when winning or whine when losing.

- Cards with [Cast] are spells from your hand. Cards with [Activate] are abilities   on permanents you control.

MULLIGAN DECISIONS:
When you see "Mulligan" in GAME_ASK, your_hand shows your current hand.
- choose_action(answer=true) means YES MULLIGAN - throw away this hand and draw new cards
- choose_action(answer=false) means NO KEEP - keep this hand and start playing
Think carefully: answer=false means KEEP, answer=true means MULLIGAN.

HOW ACTIONS WORK:
- response_type=select: Cards listed are confirmed playable with your current mana.   Play a card with choose_action(index=N). Pass with choose_action(answer=false) only   when you are done playing cards this phase.
- response_type=boolean with no playable cards: Pass with choose_action(answer=false).
- GAME_ASK (boolean): Answer true/false based on what's being asked.
- GAME_CHOOSE_ABILITY (index): Pick an ability by index.
- GAME_TARGET (index): Pick a target by index. If required=true, you must pick one.

COMBAT - ATTACKING:
When you see combat_phase="declare_attackers" in get_action_choices:
- Choices with [Attack] are creatures you can declare as attackers.   Select one with choose_action(index=N) to toggle it as an attacker.
- After selecting, call get_action_choices again to select more attackers.
- "All attack" declares all your creatures as attackers at once.
- When done selecting attackers, call choose_action(answer=true) to confirm.
- To skip attacking, call choose_action(answer=false).

COMBAT - BLOCKING:
When you see combat_phase="declare_blockers" in get_action_choices:
- "incoming_attackers" shows enemy creatures attacking you.
- Choices with [Block] are your creatures that can block.
- Select a blocker with choose_action(index=N), then you may be asked which attacker to block.
- When done selecting blockers, call choose_action(answer=true) to confirm.
- To not block, call choose_action(answer=false).

STRATEGY NOTES:
Call save_strategy(text) to save notes that persist if your context gets reset (e.g. opponent playstyles, your game plan, key threats). Max 500 chars, overwrites previous.

function.name: take_action
function.description: Execute default action (pass priority or first available choice)

function.name: send_chat_message
function.description: Send a chat message to the game

function.name: pass_priority
function.description: Auto-pass priority until you need to make a decision: playable cards, combat (declare attackers/blockers), or non-priority actions. Returns action_pending, action_type, actions_passed, has_playable_cards, combat_phase. On timeout: action_pending=false, timeout=true.

function.name: get_game_state
function.description: Get full game state: turn, phase, players, stack, combat. Each player has life, mana_pool, hand (yours only), battlefield (name, tapped, P/T, counters, token/copy/face_down flags), graveyard, exile, commanders.

function.name: get_oracle_text
function.description: Get oracle text (rules) for cards. Provide exactly one of: card_name (single), card_names (batch array), or object_id (in-game object). Single returns {name, rules}. Batch returns {cards: [{name, rules}, ...]}.

function.name: get_action_choices
function.description: Get available choices for the current pending action. Call before choose_action. Includes context (phase/turn), players (life totals), and land_drops_used (during your main phase). response_type: select (cards to play, attackers, blockers), boolean (yes/no), index (target/ability), amount, pile, or multi_amount. During combat: combat_phase indicates declare_attackers or declare_blockers.

function.name: choose_action
function.description: Respond to pending action. Use index to pick a choice (card, attacker, blocker, target, ability, mana source). Use answer for yes/no, pass priority, or confirm combat (true=confirm attackers/blockers). Call get_action_choices first.

answer.description: Yes/No response. For GAME_ASK: true means YES to the question, false means NO. For mulligan: true = YES MULLIGAN (discard hand, draw new cards), false = NO KEEP (keep this hand). For GAME_SELECT: false = pass priority (done playing cards this phase), true = confirm combat (done declaring attackers/blockers). Also false to cancel target/mana selection.

index.description: Choice index from get_action_choices (for target/ability/choice and mana source/pool choices)

text.description: Text value for GAME_CHOOSE_CHOICE (use instead of index to pick any option by name, e.g. a creature type not in the filtered list)

function.name: save_strategy
function.description: Save strategy notes that persist even if your context is reset (e.g. opponent playstyles, your game plan, key threats to track). Max 500 chars. Overwrites previous notes.

You are a competitive Magic: The Gathering player. Your goal is to WIN the game. Play to maximize your win rate — make optimal strategic decisions, not flashy or entertaining ones. Think carefully about sequencing, card evaluation, and combat math.

GAME LOOP - follow this exactly:
1. Call pass_priority - this waits until you need to make a decision    (it auto-skips phases where you have no playable cards).
2. Call get_action_choices - this shows you what you can do RIGHT NOW
3. Read the choices carefully, then call choose_action with your decision
4. Go back to step 1

CRITICAL RULES:
- ALWAYS call get_action_choices before choose_action. Never guess.
- When get_action_choices shows playable cards, you should play them before passing.   Only pass (answer=false) when you have nothing more you want to play this phase.

UNDERSTANDING get_action_choices OUTPUT:
- All cards listed in response_type=select are confirmed castable with your current mana.   The server pre-filters to only show cards you can legally play right now.
- mana_pool shows your current floating mana (e.g. {"R": 2, "W": 1}).
- untapped_lands shows how many untapped lands you control.
- Cards with [Cast] are spells from your hand. Cards with [Activate] are abilities   on permanents you control.

MULLIGAN DECISIONS:
When you see "Mulligan" in GAME_ASK, your_hand shows your current hand.
- choose_action(answer=true) means YES MULLIGAN - throw away this hand and draw new cards
- choose_action(answer=false) means NO KEEP - keep this hand and start playing
Think carefully: answer=false means KEEP, answer=true means MULLIGAN.

HOW ACTIONS WORK:
- response_type=select: Cards listed are confirmed playable with your current mana.   Play a card with choose_action(index=N). Pass with choose_action(answer=false) only   when you are done playing cards this phase.
- response_type=boolean with no playable cards: Pass with choose_action(answer=false).
- GAME_ASK (boolean): Answer true/false based on what's being asked.
- GAME_CHOOSE_ABILITY (index): Pick an ability by index.
- GAME_TARGET (index): Pick a target by index. If required=true, you must pick one.

COMBAT - ATTACKING:
When you see combat_phase="declare_attackers" in get_action_choices:
- Choices with [Attack] are creatures you can declare as attackers.   Select one with choose_action(index=N) to toggle it as an attacker.
- After selecting, call get_action_choices again to select more attackers.
- "All attack" declares all your creatures as attackers at once.
- When done selecting attackers, call choose_action(answer=true) to confirm.
- To skip attacking, call choose_action(answer=false).

COMBAT - BLOCKING:
When you see combat_phase="declare_blockers" in get_action_choices:
- "incoming_attackers" shows enemy creatures attacking you.
- Choices with [Block] are your creatures that can block.
- Select a blocker with choose_action(index=N), then you may be asked which attacker to block.
- When done selecting blockers, call choose_action(answer=true) to confirm.
- To not block, call choose_action(answer=false).

STRATEGY NOTES:
Call save_strategy(text) to save notes that persist if your context gets reset (e.g. opponent playstyles, your game plan, key threats). Max 500 chars, overwrites previous.

CHAT:
Use send_chat_message to talk to your opponents during the game. React to big plays, comment on the board state, or just have fun. Check the recent_chat field in pass_priority results to see what others are saying.

function.name: take_action
function.description: Execute default action (pass priority or first available choice)

function.name: send_chat_message
function.description: Send a chat message to the game

function.name: pass_priority
function.description: Auto-pass priority until you need to make a decision: playable cards, combat (declare attackers/blockers), or non-priority actions. Returns action_pending, action_type, actions_passed, has_playable_cards, combat_phase. On timeout: action_pending=false, timeout=true.

function.name: get_game_state
function.description: Get full game state: turn, phase, players, stack, combat. Each player has life, mana_pool, hand (yours only), battlefield (name, tapped, P/T, counters, token/copy/face_down flags), graveyard, exile, commanders.

function.name: get_oracle_text
function.description: Get oracle text (rules) for cards. Provide exactly one of: card_name (single), card_names (batch array), or object_id (in-game object). Single returns {name, rules}. Batch returns {cards: [{name, rules}, ...]}.

function.name: get_action_choices
function.description: Get available choices for the current pending action. Call before choose_action. Includes context (phase/turn), players (life totals), and land_drops_used (during your main phase). response_type: select (cards to play, attackers, blockers), boolean (yes/no), index (target/ability), amount, pile, or multi_amount. During combat: combat_phase indicates declare_attackers or declare_blockers.

function.name: choose_action
function.description: Respond to pending action. Use index to pick a choice (card, attacker, blocker, target, ability, mana source). Use answer for yes/no, pass priority, or confirm combat (true=confirm attackers/blockers). Call get_action_choices first.

answer.description: Yes/No response. For GAME_ASK: true means YES to the question, false means NO. For mulligan: true = YES MULLIGAN (discard hand, draw new cards), false = NO KEEP (keep this hand). For GAME_SELECT: false = pass priority (done playing cards this phase), true = confirm combat (done declaring attackers/blockers). Also false to cancel target/mana selection.

index.description: Choice index from get_action_choices (for target/ability/choice and mana source/pool choices)

text.description: Text value for GAME_CHOOSE_CHOICE (use instead of index to pick any option by name, e.g. a creature type not in the filtered list)

function.name: save_strategy
function.description: Save strategy notes that persist even if your context is reset (e.g. opponent playstyles, your game plan, key threats to track). Max 500 chars. Overwrites previous notes.

text.description: Strategy notes to save

function.name: get_oracle_text

function.name: get_action_choices
function.description: Get available choices for the current pending action. Call before choose_action. function.name: choose_action
function.description: Respond to pending action. Use index to pick a choice (card, attacker, blocker, target, ability, mana source). Use answer for yes/no, pass priority, or confirm combat (true=confirm attackers/blockers). Call get_action_choices first.

text.description: Text value for GAME_CHOOSE_CHOICE (use instead of index to pick any option by name, e.g. a creature type not in the filtered list)

GAME LOOP - follow this exactly:
1. Call pass_priority - this waits until you need to make a decision    (it auto-skips phases where you have no playable cards).
2. Call get_action_choices - this shows you what you can do RIGHT NOW
3. Read the choices carefully, then call choose_action with your decision
4. Go back to step 1

CRITICAL RULES:
- ALWAYS call get_action_choices before choose_action. Never guess.
- When get_action_choices shows playable cards, you should play them before passing.   Only pass (answer=false) when you have nothing more you want to play this phase.

UNDERSTANDING get_action_choices OUTPUT:
- All cards listed in response_type=select are confirmed castable with your current mana.   The server pre-filters to only show cards you can legally play right now.
- mana_pool shows your current floating mana (e.g. {"R": 2, "W": 1}).
- untapped_lands shows how many untapped lands you control.
- Cards with [Cast] are spells from your hand. Cards with [Activate] are abilities   on permanents you control.

MULLIGAN DECISIONS:
When you see "Mulligan" in GAME_ASK, your_hand shows your current hand.
- choose_action(answer=true) means YES MULLIGAN - throw away this hand and draw new cards
- choose_action(answer=false) means NO KEEP - keep this hand and start playing
Think carefully: answer=false means KEEP, answer=true means MULLIGAN.

HOW ACTIONS WORK:
- response_type=select: Cards listed are confirmed playable with your current mana.   Play a card with choose_action(index=N). Pass with choose_action(answer=false) only   when you are done playing cards this phase.
- response_type=boolean with no playable cards: Pass with choose_action(answer=false).
- GAME_ASK (boolean): Answer true/false based on what's being asked.
- GAME_CHOOSE_ABILITY (index): Pick an ability by index.
- GAME_TARGET (index): Pick a target by index. If required=true, you must pick one.

COMBAT - ATTACKING:
When you see combat_phase="declare_attackers" in get_action_choices:
- Choices with [Attack] are creatures you can declare as attackers.   Select one with choose_action(index=N) to toggle it as an attacker.
- After selecting, call get_action_choices again to select more attackers.
- "All attack" declares all your creatures as attackers at once.
- When done selecting attackers, call choose_action(answer=true) to confirm.
- To skip attacking, call choose_action(answer=false).

COMBAT - BLOCKING:
When you see combat_phase="declare_blockers" in get_action_choices:
- "incoming_attackers" shows enemy creatures attacking you.
- Choices with [Block] are your creatures that can block.
- Select a blocker with choose_action(index=N), then you may be asked which attacker to block.
- When done selecting blockers, call choose_action(answer=true) to confirm.
- To not block, call choose_action(answer=false).

STRATEGY NOTES:
Call save_strategy(text) to save notes that persist if your context gets reset (e.g. opponent playstyles, your game plan, key threats). Max 500 chars, overwrites previous.

CHAT:
Use send_chat_message to talk to your opponents during the game. React to big plays, comment on the board state, or just have fun. Check the recent_chat field in pass_priority results to see what others are saying.

function.name: pass_priority
function.description: Auto-pass priority until you need to make a decision: playable cards, combat (declare attackers/blockers), or non-priority actions. Returns action_pending, action_type, actions_passed, has_playable_cards, combat_phase. On timeout: action_pending=false, timeout=true.

function.name: get_game_state

function.name: get_oracle_text
function.description: Get oracle text (rules) for cards. Provide exactly one of: card_name (single), card_names (batch array), or object_id (in-game object). Single returns {name, rules}. Batch returns {cards: [{name, rules}, ...]}.

function.name: get_action_choices
function.description: Get available choices for the current pending action. Call before choose_action. During combat: combat_phase indicates declare_attackers or declare_blockers.

function.name: choose_action
function.description: Respond to pending action. Use index to pick a choice (card, attacker, blocker, target, ability, mana source). Use answer for yes/no, pass priority, or confirm combat (true=confirm attackers/blockers). Call get_action_choices first.

answer.description: Yes/No response. For GAME_ASK: true means YES to the question, false means NO. For mulligan: true = YES MULLIGAN (discard hand, draw new cards), false = NO KEEP (keep this hand). index.description: Choice index from get_action_choices (for target/ability/choice and mana source/pool choices)

text.description: Text value for GAME_CHOOSE_CHOICE (use instead of index to pick any option by name, e.g. a creature type not in the filtered list)

function.name: save_strategy

annotations.description: Playing Sunbillow Verge on Turn 1 when it can only produce {W} (no Mountain in play to enable its {R} ability), and the hand has no turn-1 white spells. Playing Mountain first would provide {R} mana, enabling Shock if needed on turn 1 or during the opponent's turn. On turn 2, both sequences yield the same mana access ({R}{W} or {R}{R}).
annotations.actionTaken: Played Sunbillow Verge as the Turn 1 land drop, leaving only {W} available.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain on Turn 1 to have {R} available for Shock, then play Sunbillow Verge on Turn 2 when a Mountain is in play to enable both its {W} and {R} abilities.

annotations.description: Played Steam Vents paying 2 life for untapped when Spirebluff Canal would enter untapped for free (controlling 1 other land, which is ≤ 2). Both produce the same colors. By playing Spirebluff Canal now and saving Steam Vents for turn 3, they could potentially play Steam Vents tapped on turn 3 if they don't need the mana, saving 2 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Steam Vents (paying 2 life to enter untapped)
annotations.betterLine: Play Spirebluff Canal instead, which enters untapped for free with only 1 other land, preserving the option to play Steam Vents tapped later to save 2 life

annotations.description: The player misidentified Abandon Attachments as an aura rather than an instant that discards a card to draw two. Abandon Attachments would have provided net +1 card advantage (discard 1, draw 2) compared to Accumulate Wisdom's net +0 card selection (look at 3, keep 1). Discarding Firebending Lesson would also put a Lesson in the graveyard, powering up future Accumulate Wisdom casts.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Accumulate Wisdom for card selection (net +0 cards)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Abandon Attachments, discarding Firebending Lesson or another less critical card to draw 2 (net +1 card advantage while building Lesson count in graveyard)

annotations.description: Accumulate Wisdom lets the player look at the top 3 cards and put one into hand (rest go to bottom). The choice was between Firebending Lesson, Accumulate Wisdom (another copy), and Stomping Ground. With only 2 lands on board and Monument to Endurance (3 mana) in hand, taking Stomping Ground would have enabled casting Monument on turn 3. Firebending Lesson is a situational 2-damage removal spell that costs only 1 mana and can be found later, while hitting the critical 3rd land drop on time for Monument to Endurance is more important for the game plan.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Firebending Lesson from the top 3 cards revealed by Accumulate Wisdom.
annotations.betterLine: Choose Stomping Ground to ensure the turn 3 land drop and enable casting Monument to Endurance on curve, which is a key engine piece for the deck.

annotations.description: Playing a creature in the precombat main phase when holding combat tricks (Shock, Lightning Helix) gives the opponent information unnecessarily. More importantly, the opponent's lands are both tapped, meaning there's no risk of a counter spell right now. However, the general principle of casting creatures before combat only matters when you have combat-relevant tricks, which isn't applicable here since Bashtronaut has summoning sickness. The real issue is that playing the Mountain first (from hand) before casting Bashtronaut would be better sequencing - it would leave Sunbillow Verge untapped to represent Lightning Helix (R+W) as a threat. But looking more carefully, the player hasn't played a land yet this turn and should play Mountain first to have 3 lands, then could potentially cast Lightning Helix with Mountain + Mountain + Sunbillow Verge (for W). Playing Bashtronaut first uses the Mountain, leaving only Sunbillow Verge untapped (which can only produce W), meaning they can't represent Shock. If they played Mountain first, then Bashtronaut, they'd have one untapped Mountain to represent Shock. But we don't see a land drop in this decision. The key missed opportunity is that the opponent's lands are tapped - this was actually a fine time to deploy Bashtronaut. The play is reasonable.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Burnout Bashtronaut in precombat main
annotations.betterLine: Should have played Mountain from hand first (land drop), then cast Burnout Bashtronaut, leaving an extra untapped Mountain to represent Shock on the opponent's turn

annotations.description: Cast Artist's Talent instead of killing Burnout Bashtronaut with Firebending Lesson while holding up It'll Quench Ya! countermagic. The Bashtronaut has menace and the speed mechanic that makes it increasingly dangerous, and removing it for R while keeping counterspell backup (1U) is a cleaner tempo play on turn 3.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Artist's Talent for 1R, leaving only 1 mana open (not enough for It'll Quench Ya!)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Firebending Lesson targeting Burnout Bashtronaut (kills the 1/1), leaving 2 mana open for It'll Quench Ya! to counter any turn 3 play from opponent

annotations.description: Let Artist's Talent resolve when opponent was completely tapped out and couldn't pay for It'll Quench Ya!'s tax of {2}. Artist's Talent is a powerful engine card providing card filtering and eventually cost reduction and damage amplification. With 3 untapped lands, could have also killed Burnout Bashtronaut with Firebending Lesson in the same turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, allowing Artist's Talent to resolve unchallenged.
annotations.betterLine: Cast It'll Quench Ya! targeting Artist's Talent (opponent tapped out, can't pay {2}), and optionally also cast Firebending Lesson targeting Burnout Bashtronaut to remove the threat. Had exactly 3 mana for both plays.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Firebending Lesson to kill Burnout Bashtronaut (1/1) while having one untapped red source with no useful instant-speed play available. The Bashtronaut scales with speed mechanics and gains double strike at max speed. Holding R open serves no purpose since It'll Quench Ya requires 1U and no other meaningful instant is castable. Casting Firebending Lesson would also trigger Artist's Talent for card filtering.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting, keeping one red mana open with no useful way to spend it.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Firebending Lesson targeting Burnout Bashtronaut to remove the scaling threat, triggering Artist's Talent for a discard-draw cycle.

annotations.description: Casting Firebending Lesson during combat (before declaring attackers) to kill Burnout Bashtronaut is a reasonable removal play, but the timing is slightly suboptimal. The opponent's lands are all tapped, so there's no risk of pump activations. However, casting it now during combat rather than during the main phase means the Artist's Talent trigger (discard to draw) happens here. The real question is whether holding the Firebending Lesson for later would have been better, since Burnout Bashtronaut is only a 1/1 with menace at speed 1 and isn't an immediate major threat. Using a removal spell on a 1/1 when the opponent has tapped out could be premature, though preventing speed from increasing has value.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Firebending Lesson to deal 2 damage to Burnout Bashtronaut during combat phase
annotations.betterLine: This is a reasonable play to prevent the Bashtronaut from gaining speed and becoming a double-striker. However, waiting could have preserved the removal for a more impactful threat like Nova Hellkite. The play is defensible but debatable.

annotations.description: Lightning Helix cannot target Artist's Talent (an enchantment) - it can only target creatures and players. The reasoning suggests targeting Artist's Talent, but that's not a valid target. Going face with Lightning Helix for 3 damage + 3 life is fine value, but the player should have played the Sunbillow Verge land from hand first before casting spells. Playing the land first costs nothing and ensures the mana is available for future turns. Additionally, with the opponent tapped out, Shock (1 mana) to face leaves 2 mana open, which could be more flexible than committing 2 mana to Lightning Helix now when there's nothing urgent to remove.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lightning Helix before playing Sunbillow Verge from hand
annotations.betterLine: Play Sunbillow Verge first, then decide between Lightning Helix or Shock to the opponent's face. Playing the land before casting spells is strictly better sequencing.

annotations.description: Lightning Helix costs {R}{W}. The two Mountains can provide {R}, so Sunbillow Verge needs to provide {W} to pay for the spell. Choosing to add {R} instead of {W} means the white mana requirement cannot be met, potentially causing the spell to fail or requiring incorrect mana payment.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Sunbillow Verge to add {R}
annotations.betterLine: Activate Sunbillow Verge to add {W} to pay for Lightning Helix's white mana cost

annotations.description: The player should play Sunbillow Verge from hand before casting spells. Playing land first is proper sequencing - it ensures the land drop isn't forgotten and provides additional mana for potential follow-up plays this turn (e.g., after Warp-casting Nova Hellkite for 3 mana, the 4th land could enable Lightning Helix with the remaining mana).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Nova Hellkite (via Warp for {2}{R}) before playing the Sunbillow Verge land from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Sunbillow Verge first, then Warp Nova Hellkite for {2}{R} using two Mountains, leaving Sunbillow Verge + Mountain untapped to potentially cast Lightning Helix ({R}{W}) if needed after combat.

annotations.description: Cast Stormchaser's Talent before playing Mountain from hand. With Mountain played first, they would have 3 mana available and could cast both Stormchaser's Talent (U) AND Accumulate Wisdom (1U), which with 4 Lesson cards in graveyard draws 3 cards instead of 1. By casting before the land drop, they likely miss out on casting both spells this turn, losing massive card advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Stormchaser's Talent for U before playing land, leaving only 1 untapped mana
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain first to have 3 untapped lands, then cast both Stormchaser's Talent (U) and Accumulate Wisdom (1U) to create a 1/1 prowess token AND draw 3 cards

annotations.description: Cast Nova Hellkite via Warp ({2}{R}) before playing a land, leaving 0 mana open. Should have played Mountain first to have 1 mana available after casting, potentially enabling Shock as interaction on the opponent's turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Nova Hellkite via Warp for {2}{R} with only 3 lands, using all mana and leaving 0 open.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain first, then cast Nova Hellkite via Warp, leaving 1 mana open for Shock if needed.

annotations.description: Cast Lightning Helix before playing a land. With only one Sunbillow Verge on the battlefield, they have only one white mana source, meaning they can only cast one Lightning Helix this turn. By playing the second Sunbillow Verge from hand first, they would have had two white sources and could cast both Lightning Helixes in the same turn for 6 damage (8→2hp). The player's reasoning also incorrectly states Lightning Helix deals 2 damage when it deals 3.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lightning Helix before playing a land for the turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Sunbillow Verge first, then cast both Lightning Helixes (4 mana: RRWW available from 3 Mountains + 2 Sunbillow Verges) to deal 6 damage this turn

annotations.description: Tapped Sunbillow Verge for {R} instead of {W} while Lightning Helix ({R}{W}) is on the stack. Sunbillow Verge is their only white mana source, so tapping it for red means they cannot produce the {W} needed to pay for Lightning Helix.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Sunbillow Verge for {R} while needing {W} to cast Lightning Helix
annotations.betterLine: Activate Sunbillow Verge for {W} and use a Mountain for the {R} to properly pay for Lightning Helix

annotations.description: Haiku Stoic cast Lightning Helix before playing a land. They have Mountain and Sunbillow Verge in hand, and could play Mountain first to have 5 lands available. While they can cast Lightning Helix with current mana (needing RW, having 3 Mountains + Sunbillow Verge for 4 mana), playing the land first would leave more mana open after casting the Helix. With 5 lands they'd have 3 mana remaining after Helix instead of 2, giving more flexibility for future plays or if they draw something. Additionally, the opponent is at 8 life and two Lightning Helixes deal 6 damage total — this doesn't kill the opponent yet, so sequencing land first is strictly better to maximize open mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lightning Helix before playing a land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain first, then cast Lightning Helix, leaving 3 mana open instead of 2.

annotations.description: Gem25F Analyst declined to counter Lightning Helix with It'll Quench Ya! while at 8 life. Lightning Helix deals 3 damage AND gains the opponent 3 life, representing a 6-point life swing. At 8 life, taking 3 puts them to 5, which is extremely dangerous against a red deck. They had 2 untapped lands (Spirebluff Canal and Willowrush Verge) which could produce the {1}{U} needed to cast It'll Quench Ya!. The opponent has 4 lands but only 4 Mountains/Sunbillow Verge visible, and with Lightning Helix on the stack they've already used mana this turn, so paying {2} for the tax is unlikely. Even if the opponent could pay, forcing them to spend 2 additional mana is still valuable. The reasoning about 'holding it for something dangerous' is wrong — at 8 life, a 3-damage spell that also gains the opponent 3 life IS the dangerous thing.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast It'll Quench Ya! to counter Lightning Helix, letting it resolve and taking 3 damage (going to 5 life) while opponent gained 3 life (going to 23).
annotations.betterLine: Cast It'll Quench Ya! targeting Lightning Helix to counter it (or at minimum tax the opponent 2 mana). Preserving 3 life points and denying 3 life gain at 8 life is critical.

annotations.description: Failed to play Sunbillow Verge from hand, which would have provided the white mana needed to cast Lightning Helix this turn. With opponent at 5 life, Lightning Helix would deal 3 damage (putting opponent to 2 life) and gain 3 life. Missing a land drop that enables a key spell against a low-life opponent is a significant mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to play a land, leaving Lightning Helix uncastable due to no untapped white source.
annotations.betterLine: Play Sunbillow Verge (which enters untapped since they control a Mountain), then cast Lightning Helix targeting the opponent to deal 3 damage (opponent to 2 life) and gain 3 life.

annotations.description: Haiku Stoic declined to play a land when they have two lands in hand and open land drops available. With the opponent at 5 life and Lightning Helix in hand (which costs RW and deals 3 damage), having access to more mana sources is important. Playing a Mountain or Sunbillow Verge costs nothing and provides additional mana for future turns. Missing a land drop is pure downside with no strategic benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to play a land during postcombat main phase despite having Mountain and Sunbillow Verge in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain (or Sunbillow Verge) to have 5 lands available next turn, maximizing mana for casting Lightning Helix plus any other spells, or activating abilities.

annotations.description: Cast Monument to Endurance before playing a land drop. More importantly, leveling Artist's Talent to Level 2 (cost {2}{R}) was likely a stronger play here - it would reduce the cost of all noncreature spells by {1}, making It'll Quench Ya! cost just {U} and other spells cheaper. At 5 HP, mana efficiency for reactive spells is critical. Additionally, casting before playing a land is a sequencing error even though it doesn't change available mana here.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Monument to Endurance for 3 mana before playing a land
annotations.betterLine: Play a land (Island or Mountain) first, then activate Artist's Talent Level 2 for {2}{R}, leaving mana open for cheaper counterspells and burn going forward

annotations.description: Discarded Abandon Attachments (a useful card advantage spell, especially synergistic with Monument to Endurance's discard triggers and Artist's Talent) instead of one of their excess lands. The player had 4 lands in play and 4 lands in hand, far more than needed.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Abandon Attachments to Artist's Talent's loot trigger
annotations.betterLine: Discard a redundant land like Willowrush Verge or Riverpyre Verge, keeping Abandon Attachments as a card advantage spell that synergizes with Monument to Endurance (on the stack) and Artist's Talent's discard triggers.

annotations.description: Willowrush Verge produces U or G, but the player has no green cards. Riverpyre Verge produces U or R, which is strictly more useful given the deck's UR color identity and cards in hand like Firebending Lesson (R).
annotations.actionTaken: Played Willowrush Verge, gaining a redundant U/G source when they already had one Willowrush Verge on board.
annotations.betterLine: Play Riverpyre Verge instead to maximize red mana availability, enabling more flexible sequencing of Firebending Lesson and other red spells alongside blue counterspells.

annotations.description: Haiku Stoic has no nonland permanents, so Boomerang Basics can only target Gem25F Analyst's own permanents. Bouncing your own key permanent (like Monument to Endurance or Artist's Talent) for a card draw is a significant tempo loss. Meanwhile, leveling Artist's Talent to Level 2 for {2}{R} (exactly the 3 untapped mana available) would reduce all noncreature spell costs by {1}, enabling far more efficient future turns at a critical 5 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Boomerang Basics with no opponent nonland permanents to target, forced to bounce own permanent
annotations.betterLine: Activate Artist's Talent to Level 2 for {2}{R}, gaining the cost reduction ability to cast future spells more efficiently

annotations.description: Bounced Artist's Talent which has no ETB trigger, missing the opportunity to bounce Stormchaser's Talent which would create a 1/1 Otter token with prowess when replayed. At 5 life, generating a blocker is extremely valuable, and the Otter token is free extra value from the bounce.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Artist's Talent with Boomerang Basics
annotations.betterLine: Target Stormchaser's Talent with Boomerang Basics to get the draw from bouncing your own permanent AND create another 1/1 prowess Otter when replayed, providing a much-needed blocker at 5 life.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 3 life and Haiku Stoic has Lightning Helix in hand, which deals 3 damage to any target. With 4 Mountains already on the battlefield (one tapped Sunbillow Verge + 3 Mountains), they have access to at least 3 untapped Mountains producing RRR, which is enough to cast Lightning Helix (RW). Sunbillow Verge can produce W when untapped. Wait - Sunbillow Verge is tapped. But they have 3 untapped Mountains. Lightning Helix costs {R}{W} - they need a white source. Sunbillow Verge is tapped. Playing Mountain doesn't help cast Lightning Helix since they still lack an untapped white source. Playing Sunbillow Verge would give them an untapped white source (it can tap for W if they control a Mountain, which they do). This would let them cast Lightning Helix this turn to deal exactly lethal 3 damage to the opponent at 3 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain instead of Sunbillow Verge, leaving no untapped white mana source to cast Lightning Helix for lethal.
annotations.betterLine: Play Sunbillow Verge (which enters untapped and can tap for W since they control Mountains), then cast Lightning Helix targeting the opponent for exactly 3 damage lethal.

annotations.description: At 3 life with 6 untapped lands, casting Abandon Attachments before Gran-Gran wastes 1 mana. Gran-Gran's cost reduction is immediately active (8 Lesson cards in graveyard), making all noncreature spells cost {1} less. Additionally, a land should be played first. The player's reasoning was confused, attributing abilities to Abandon Attachments that it doesn't have.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Abandon Attachments for {1}{U/R} (2 mana) before deploying Gran-Gran or playing a land
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (Island/Mountain/Riverpyre Verge), then cast Gran-Gran for {U} to activate cost reduction, then cast Abandon Attachments for just {U/R} (1 mana with discount), leaving more mana open for It'll Quench Ya! or other spells

annotations.description: With 8 cards already in hand, drawing yet another card provides diminishing returns compared to a Treasure token that could help deploy more of the existing hand this turn. At 3 life, tempo and board development are critical.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose 'Draw a card' from Monument to Endurance trigger
annotations.betterLine: Choose 'Create a Treasure token' to help cast more spells from the already-large hand, improving tempo when at critically low life

annotations.description: At 3 life with 3 untapped lands, casting Boomerang Basics for 1 mana to bounce own permanent and draw is fine, but they had 2 mana remaining afterward and could have also deployed Artist's Talent for additional card filtering value. They appear to have passed without using their remaining mana. Additionally, bouncing Monument to Endurance (their main value engine) rather than Stormchaser's Talent (which could be replayed to create another Otter token with prowess for blocking) may have been the wrong target.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Boomerang Basics (likely bouncing own Monument to Endurance) without casting Artist's Talent with remaining 2 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Boomerang Basics bouncing Stormchaser's Talent (to replay later for another Otter), then cast Artist's Talent with remaining 2 mana for ongoing card filtering, which is critical when at 3 life.

annotations.description: The opponent is at 3 life and Haiku Stoic has Lightning Helix in hand, which deals 3 damage to any target. This is immediate lethal that doesn't require combat or give the opponent any chance to interact with a creature. Instead, they chose to cast Nova Hellkite (likely with Warp, which exiles it at end of turn), giving the opponent a chance to counter it or find answers. The opponent has 3 untapped lands (Spirebluff Canal, Willowrush Verge, Willowrush Verge) and could potentially have countermagic like It'll Quench Ya!. Lightning Helix costs RW and Haiku Stoic has Sunbillow Verge (which can produce W if controlling a Mountain, which they do) plus Mountains for R, so they can cast it.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Nova Hellkite instead of using Lightning Helix for lethal damage.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning Helix targeting the opponent for 3 damage, winning the game immediately with no chance for interaction beyond a hard counter (which is less likely to stop a 2-mana spell than a larger creature spell).

annotations.description: Opponent is at 3 life and Haiku Stoic has Lightning Helix in hand (deals 3 damage to any target), which is exactly lethal. Instead of tapping Sunbillow Verge for {W} to cast Lightning Helix for the kill, they tapped it for {R} to cast Nova Hellkite from exile, missing lethal damage.

annotations.betterLine: Tap Sunbillow Verge for {W}, tap one Mountain for {R}, cast Lightning Helix targeting the opponent for exactly 3 lethal damage.
